_README: Field reference for a TAPPaaS satellite instance (ADR-010 §8.4): ~/config/<instance>.json, written by `module-manager module add satellite` (a satellite from before §8.4 is ~/config/satellite-<name>.json). A satellite is its own machine (kind=machine, ADR-022f), NOT a Proxmox cluster:vm. General module fields (address, roles, management, rebootOk, physicalLocation, zone0) are in module-fields.json; this file adds the satellite's own. PRINCIPLE: only operator-facing choices; every derived value (tunnel, ports, per-role tuning, backup mechanics) is defaulted by the module (lib/provision.sh) — see 'derived' below. Secrets are never stored here.

moduleSource.note: absolute path of the satellite module's directory (src/foundation/satellite) — written by module add, backfilled on satellites from before ADR-010 §8.4 by migration 0008; what module_of and `module list --resolution` name the module by (#609 renamed it from location)

values.machine: its own system with an OS, provisioned by the satellite module (ADR-010 §8, ADR-022f D2) — only value; was external-host before #611

values.foundation: foundation-grade but OPTIONAL (not in the mandatory install chain)

name.description: the name the OPNsense side knows it by (server tappaas-edge-<name>, peer tappaas-<name>); defaults to the instance name. A satellite from before §8.4 keeps its own (e.g. satellite1).

values.debian: ADR-010 Option 3 (default): stock Debian 12/13 provisioned over SSH by the module (no nixos-anywhere); official proxmox-backup-server for the backup role; OS diversity protects the vault from a nixpkgs supply-chain compromise (§7.3)
values.nixos: declarative NixOS via nixos-anywhere (satellite.nix); patches itself, so recorded unmanaged

values.admin-vpn: blind UDP relay of an admin WireGuard session terminating on OPNsense (`network-manager wgvpn`)
values.backup: off-site PBS pull vault — set by `module modify <instance> --lockdown`, refused at add

roles.note: a general module field (module-fields.json); default [reverse-proxy, admin-vpn]

dependsOn.note: EMPTY: nothing the satellite needs is a service another module provides. It needs OPNsense (network) and tappaas-cicd, present on every Site.

values.generic: operator supplies a host + SSH; no API automation

values.portal: Tier A (default): operator creates the VPS in the console
values.api: Tier B (opt-in): TAPPaaS creates it via the hcloud API token

provider.location.note: Tier B (allocation=api) ONLY — hcloud region for `hcloud server create`. For Tier A you pick it in the console (the module does not use it).

provider.serverType.note: Tier B (allocation=api) ONLY — x86 cx23 default; cax11 = ARM. For Tier A you pick it in the console.

physicalLocation.country.note: ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country the satellite physically runs in (#609, ADR-012 §1.5) — the evidence its backup copy is off-site. NOT provider.location, which is only a provisioning parameter. `backup-manager validate` warns while it is missing.

physicalLocation.city.note: needed to show separation from a Site in the same country

physicalLocation.building.note: data centre or building — needed when it shares the Site's city

fields._provider_image: dropped — the image is irrelevant (Debian is provisioned in place; nixos-anywhere reformats any stock image); the module defaults it for Tier B.

host.publicIp.note: before ADR-010 §8.4: the public address. Now the general `address` field (given at add, --address); still read when `address` is absent.

host.operatorSshKeys.note: the operator's out-of-band root key(s) — recorded at install from the forwarded agent or TAPPAAS_OPERATOR_KEY; never the mothership's key, which a managed satellite authorizes separately and --lockdown removes (§8.4)

vault.datastore.name.note: the vault (backup role, after --lockdown) — `vault`, not `backup`, which is every module's backup policy; a config from before §8.4 had these under `backup`, still read; local PBS datastore that receives the pull (default local ZFS/dir)

vault.datastore.path.note: the vault (backup role, after --lockdown); datastore path (put on a ZFS dataset for a real vault — create the pool on the host first)

vault.pull.homePbsHost.note: the vault (backup role, after --lockdown); HOME PBS address reachable over the tunnel (the satellite PULLS from it). Added to wg AllowedIPs + an OPNsense edge->PBS:8007 rule.

vault.pull.homeDatastore.note: the vault (backup role, after --lockdown); the home datastore to pull

vault.pull.authId.note: the vault (backup role, after --lockdown); the READ-ONLY home PBS API token id. The token SECRET is out-of-band (TAPPAAS_SAT_PBS_TOKEN[_FILE]), NEVER in this JSON (§7).

vault.pull.fingerprint.note: the vault (backup role, after --lockdown); home PBS TLS cert fingerprint

vault.pull.schedule.note: the vault (backup role, after --lockdown); pull sync-job schedule (PBS calendar event)

vault.s3.note: OPTIONAL alternative backend (endpoint/bucket) instead of a local ZFS datastore. NOTE: PBS does NOT support S3 Object Lock — enabling it CORRUPTS the datastore (Bugzilla #6780). Immutability comes from the PULL model, not Object Lock.

derived._note: NOT operator config — the module (lib/provision.sh) computes these with sensible defaults and renders them into the Debian config files (or satellite-settings.nix). Listed here for reference only.
derived.tunnel: satelliteAddr/homeAddr = a dedicated /31 (default 10.255.0.0/31, auto-allocated per satellite); wgPort 51820 (config knob only if hostile egress needs 443/udp); PersistentKeepalive 25
derived.reverseProxy: forwarder nginx stream; :80 redirect via Caddy; SNI '*' (single-site passthrough); proxyProtocol off until the Caddy side supports it (§2)
derived.adminVpn: terminates on OPNsense (always) into the admin overlay zone; adminWgPort 51821; admin-side MTU ~1340
derived.backup: PULL model (Debian satellite runs official PBS, pulls from home over the tunnel, owns prune/GC); --remove-vanished false; client-side encryption key stays home (§3.2); local datastore (default ZFS) into namespace remote/<name>; immutability = pull direction + destination-owned retention (NOT S3 Object Lock — PBS can't do it, #6780)
derived.update: managed (default): the nightly sweep patches it (the debianhost update; reboots per rebootOk), unattended-upgrades off. unmanaged (after --lockdown): security-only unattended-upgrades with a reboot window; the cluster holds no key (§7.3, §8.4)
